notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 21. My tool access ran out before a single page loaded, so I haven't read anything from the approved sites.

On the first try I asked for eight commentary pages at once: Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry, Augustine on New Advent, NET Bible notes and Precept Austin. That hit the tool's usage limit. When I tried again with fewer pages, I was told I had no tool calls left for this turn.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. Since I found nothing, I have nothing to report. I'm not going to write the notes from my own memory and attach URLs I never opened, because that would break your rules.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll fetch the sources a few at a time to stay under the limit, in this order:
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, then Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on BibleHub. If there's room, I'll add Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*, Matthew Henry, Barnes and Precept Austin.
2. **Differences between Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, plus Lutheran (LCMS or 1517) and Reformed pages that discuss Psalm 21. One likely topic is whether the king is David alone or a picture of Christ, especially in verses 4–6 where he is given "life… forever and ever".
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes on the Hebrew of verses 4, 9 and 12. For Augustine, note that he numbers the Psalms the old Latin way, so our Psalm 21 is his Psalm 20. I'll also look for any pages discussing prosperity-style readings of verse 2, "You have granted his heart's desire", and only include that if a source actually covers it.
